# Mechanical Keyboard

## Overview

A 65% aluminium board with a gasket mount, built over a weekend. I wanted something quieter than the stock plastic case and small enough to sit next to a trackpad without pushing my mouse halfway off the desk. Linear switches, no click, because I type near other people. The whole thing weighs about 1.1 kg and does not slide around even during a fast paragraph. Keycaps are double-shot PBT with a slightly textured top. I picked a neutral grey finish so it does not look out of place next to a laptop.

## Setup

I lubed the switches with Krytox 205g0, a thin coat on the stem and a touch on the spring so it does not ping. Springs are 65 g, heavier than stock, which stops accidental keypresses when I rest my hands on the board. Case foam sits between the plate and the PCB to kill the hollow resonance. It uses 5-pin hotswap sockets, so nothing is soldered; I test each switch before pressing it in. QMK layers: a base layer, a function layer for media and arrows, and a numpad layer on the right hand for numbers. I flashed the firmware over the keyboard's own bootloader and keep the map in a text file.

## Maintenance

Every few months I pull the keycaps and dust the plate with a soft brush. Sticky switches get a drop of lube on the stem rails. The case screws get a gentle check so the foam does not compress and rattle. If a socket feels loose I reseat the switch with a puller and make sure no pin is bent. Small things, but they keep it feeling new.
